overview.description: Cockroach Poker is a commercial bluffing card game where players pass creature cards while declaring what they claim the card is.

history.origins: Designed by Jacques Zeimet and published by Drei Magier Spiele in 2004, Cockroach Poker is a modern bluffing party card game.
timeline: Documented card-play form: Cockroach Poker is described as a distinct game with its own rules.

setup.players: 2-6 players use the table arrangement described for Cockroach Poker.
setup.equipment: Dedicated Cockroach Poker creature deck, score area, and enough table space for play.
setup.dealing: Deal the creature cards among players; there is no shared rank-and-suit deck.

rules.objective: Avoid collecting four cards of the same creature type or otherwise becoming the single loser.
rules.gameplay: A player passes a facedown card with a claim. The receiver may accept and judge true or false, or peek and pass it onward with a claim. The wrong player keeps the card.
keyRules: Claims may be true or false.
A receiver may challenge or pass onward.
Four of a kind usually loses.

ante.reason: Beggar My Neighbour is a children's game of chance and does not utilize a monetary or chip-based ante.

deal.reason: The entire deck is distributed equally by the system dealer at the start of the game session.

reveal_market.reason: This is a closed-stack accumulation game where all cards are held in private stacks; no market exists.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase or swap cards from any shared area; they only play from their own stack.

buy_stock.reason: There is no remaining stock after the initial deal; every card is in a player's stack.

fold.reason: Participation is mandatory for every turn until a player's stack is completely exhausted.

check.reason: The game follows a deterministic flip-and-pay structure rather than a vying structure with checks.

call.reason: There are no bets to match in this game; competition is based on card accumulation through face-card triggers.

bet.reason: Success is determined by collecting the physical cards rather than wagering points or currency.

raise.reason: There is no wagering mechanic in this game, so raising stakes is not a valid action.

declare.reason: The results of each card flip are immediate and public; no separate declaration phase is required.

reveal_hand.reason: Stacks remain face down; only the top card is revealed when played onto the central pile.

award_pot.reason: While players win the center pile, it is not a pot of chips; it is handled by Outcome A/B logic.

play_card.description: Flip the top card of your stack onto the center pile.
play_card.constraints: Must be your turn or your obligation to pay.

draw.reason: New cards are only acquired by winning the central pile through successful face-card triggers.

discard.reason: Every card remains in play until collected by a player or the game terminates; no discarding exists.

pass.reason: Players cannot skip their turn to flip or pay; the sequence of actions is strictly forced.

bid.reason: Beggar My Neighbour does not utilize a bidding system to determine game state or dealer.

meld.reason: This is an accumulation game based on single card flips rather than building sets or sequences.

go_out.reason: A player exits the game only when their stack is empty; the round terminates for the loser.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: Cards are only moved from player stacks to the center and back; no drawing from a stock pile occurs.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards played to the center are part of the active pile to be won; no discard or waste pile exists.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Face cards trigger payment obligations (Ace=4, King=3, etc.); these are modeled in game logic rather than as separate special card actions.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: The result of each flip is immediate and public; no hidden declaration phase exists.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Beggar My Neighbour is an accumulation game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.
notApplicableReasons.shedding: Goal is to win all cards from others; players play from stacks rather than emptying a hand as in shedding games.

customActions.description: Move the top card of the player stack to the central pile.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; only the presence of face cards (Ace, King, Queen, Jack) determines play flow.
engine.deckDescription: Deck used for Cockroach Poker: Dedicated Cockroach Poker creature deck. Use the ranks, suits, special cards, and pack size described in the setup section for this catalog record.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits are present in the pack, but suits have no rule effect because the cards are only scattered and collected.
engine.rankDescription: The standard ranks ace through king are present in the pack, but ranks have no rule effect in this social prank.
engine.dealPattern: No deal; the whole pack is scattered after the invitation is accepted.
